book.why: This is Ophelia's cleanest expression of her lead energy call: it has record cracks, a ~$6 Brent-WTI spread from the Hormuz and Sheskharis supply shock and the strongest 12-week trend on the sheet (+38.9%), and energy's -0.43 correlation to SPY protects the book if the minutes or Warsh turn hawkish.

This is Cecil's cleanest value pick, a top-tier insurer on the lowest trailing P/E on the sheet (11.1x) with EPS still growing 10.1%, bought after a -2.7% week and largely unaffected by this week's retail reports or consumer data.

Marky's top score (83/100) is the only one of his five with both a dip deeper than one channel width and a weekly MACD histogram already turning up; it sits 1.2 widths below the line of a 26-week channel rising 18% a year, well inside the 2.5-width break, and last week's +7.1% confirms the turn.

This is the direct expression of Ophelia's tech call ahead of the Aug 26 report, which comes after this week's close, and her own offset if the oil premium drains; the sheet puts it at 100% of its 52-week high rather than the 4.8% below she cites, so it is held for the run-up to earnings, not as a dip.

GS is cheap for its growth at 16.0x trailing against 43.9% EPS growth and is a sound franchise; it is the laggard way into the financials breakout (+4.7% over 12 weeks against JPM's 19%) and the steadiest name in the book at 2.98% weekly volatility.

rationale: No name was picked by two members, so there is no double-backed anchor; the book takes each member's strongest pick by their own test, balancing Ophelia's energy lead (VLO) against her own tech offset (NVDA) and Marky's top-ranked turn (MOD), with two of Cecil's cheap, sound financials (PGR, GS) as ballast. Where members disagree: energy stays because Cecil's objections (chasing a +7.7% week, refiners above target) are about price, not a verdict on the sector call, but only one energy name is held and COP is the alternate; REGN is out because a PDUFA decision around Wednesday is a coin flip, not an expression of the defensive, 0.5-beta healthcare call it was picked to carry. GS takes Cecil's second slot over NEM, whose case leans on record gold and a one-off Barrick windfall after a +31% month, and Cecil's objection to GOOGL is a value test that does not apply to a chart pick, so GOOGL stays as Marky's alternate behind his higher-scoring MOD. The book is fully invested because its hedges sit in the names (energy's -0.43 correlation to SPY, an 11x insurer) and no member argued for cash; I have no memory of how this week went and used only logs.md and sheet.csv.
